messages.content:
Quantum entanglement is when two particles become connected in such a way that measuring one instantly affects the other, no matter how far apart they are. If you measure one particle's spin as "up," its entangled partner will instantly be "down" - not because information traveled between them, but because they share a single quantum state that only becomes definite when measured.

It's not useful for faster-than-light communication (you can't control what result you get), but it's real, experimentally verified, and genuinely strange - Einstein called it "spooky action at a distance" because he was uncomfortable with it, though it turned out to be how nature actually works.
